nodes.name: Hora dipterocarp
nodes.desc: A giant endemic rainforest tree, up to about 40 to 45 m tall, with winged seeds carried by wind. It grows in the wet lowlands including Sinharaja, where dipterocarps dominate the valleys and lower slopes.

nodes.name: Wild figs
nodes.desc: Fig trees fruit through much of the year in tropical forests and are a widely used food for fruit-eating birds and monkeys.

nodes.name: Malabar melastome
nodes.desc: A common flowering shrub of forest clearings and edges. GloBI records show bulbuls eating its fruit.

nodes.name: Jaggery palm
nodes.desc: A fishtail palm recorded in the reserve; local people tap its sap, and its fruit and flowers feed forest animals.

nodes.name: Purple-faced langur
nodes.desc: A mostly leaf-eating monkey of closed-canopy wet-zone forest that also eats fruit, flowers and seeds. Its range is now small and fragmented.

nodes.name: Toque macaque
nodes.desc: An omnivorous monkey of Sri Lanka that eats fruit, seeds and insects.

nodes.name: Sri Lankan giant squirrel
nodes.desc: A large tree squirrel of the forest canopy that feeds on fruit, seeds and bark.

nodes.name: Green imperial pigeon
nodes.desc: A large fruit-eating pigeon of forest canopy that swallows fruit whole, especially figs.

nodes.name: Red-vented bulbul
nodes.desc: A well-recorded songbird that eats fruit and insects. GloBI records include it eating Melastoma and being eaten by the green vine snake.

nodes.name: Forest insects
nodes.desc: Leaf-eating insects, beetles, crickets and other small invertebrates that feed on leaves and litter and are prey for lizards, frogs and birds.

nodes.name: Sri Lanka drongo
nodes.desc: An insect-eating bird that hunts from open perches. Related drongos are noisy members of the mixed-species flocks that Sinharaja is known for.

nodes.name: Sri Lanka blue magpie
nodes.desc: An endemic forest bird that eats mainly insects, frogs and small lizards, plus some fruit, and may take eggs or chicks of other birds.

nodes.name: Green forest lizard
nodes.desc: A common agamid lizard of the wet zone that feeds on insects.

nodes.name: Hour-glass tree frog
nodes.desc: A common tree frog of Sri Lanka that eats insects at night.

nodes.name: Green vine snake
nodes.desc: A slender tree snake that eats lizards and frogs. GloBI records show it eating red-vented bulbuls.

nodes.name: Common water monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard that eats frogs and other small animals, and also scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Sri Lankan leopard
nodes.desc: The island apex predator, living in forests across Sri Lanka. It hunts monkeys and other mammals, and no larger carnivore competes with it.

nodes.name: Tropical sunlight
nodes.desc: Year-round warmth and light drive the forest canopy.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Roughly 3,600 to 5,000 mm of rain per year falls in two monsoons, keeping the forest wet all year.

nodes.name: Rainforest soil
nodes.desc: Nutrients held in thin, wet soils are recycled quickly from fallen leaves and dead wood.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & litter fauna
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
